analysis.title: Weekly Headings Snapshot (Week Ending October 30, 2026)
key_insights: Raymond James outlines its base case for the midterm election and what the results could mean for the market outlook.
Since 1950, November and December has been the strongest two-month period for the S&P 500, averaging +3%.
3Q GDP grew 3.4% QoQ, driven by consumer spending (+3.8%) and private investment (+19.4%).
The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75%-4.00%, with two FOMC members dissenting in favor of a 25 bp rate hike.
Lula da Silva was unexpectedly reelected as Brazil's president, and the Brazilian real had its sharpest daily decline since 1999.
ISM Manufacturing (Mon 11/2) and ISM Services (Wed 11/4) are both expected to remain in expansion.
Midterm Election Day is Tuesday 11/3, determining the composition of the House and Senate for the next two years.
Raymond James expects October job growth in Friday's BLS employment report to accelerate from 29k in September to about 70k, which it describes as a healthy and stable labor market.
Week ending 10/29 index moves: S&P 500 +0.8% (+13.8% YTD), Russell 2000 +2.7% (+16.3% YTD), Russell MidCap +1.4%, Emerging Markets +1.1%, AC World +0.9%, BG Commodity -0.9% (+28.9% YTD).
